questions.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -3 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ -3 & -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of ${a}_{31}$ equal to zero.*
questions.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the right of ${a}_{31}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -3 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ -3 & -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-2){C}_{1} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-3){C}_{1} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+2{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & -9 & 3 \\ -1 & 3 & 7 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 4 & 10 & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & -9 & 3 \\ -1 & 3 & 7 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 4 & 10 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+1}|\begin{aligned}-5 & -9 & 3 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 \\ 4 & 10 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-5 & -9 & 3 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 \\ 4 & 10 & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
|\begin{aligned}8 & -4 & 7 & -3 \\ 2 & -4 & -5 & 4 \\ -2 & 4 & -8 & 2 \\ 5 & 3 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left of ${a}_{34}$ equal to zero.*
questions.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left of ${a}_{34}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}8 & -4 & 7 & -3 \\ 2 & -4 & -5 & 4 \\ -2 & 4 & -8 & 2 \\ 5 & 3 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{4} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-2){C}_{4} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+4{C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -5 & -3 \\ 6 & -12 & 11 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -5 & -3 \\ 6 & -12 & 11 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+4}|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -5 \\ 6 & -12 & 11 \\ 3 & 7 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -5 \\ 6 & -12 & 11 \\ 3 & 7 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

|\begin{aligned}9 & 8 & -4 & -3 \\ 5 & -4 & -1 & 3 \\ -3 & 0 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & -6 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}|

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

questions.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left of ${a}_{44}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}9 & 8 & -4 & -3 \\ 5 & -4 & -1 & 3 \\ -3 & 0 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & -6 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{4} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+3{C}_{4} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-2){C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}6 & -1 & 2 & -3 \\ 8 & 5 & -7 & 3 \\ -4 & -3 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Calculate the value of 
$\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -2 & 5 \\ 5 & -6 & 4 & 1 \\ 4 & -4 & 2 & -2 \\ -6 & 1 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*
questions.worked_solution:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}=2$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & -2 & 5 \\ 5 & -6 & 4 & 1 \\ 4 & -4 & 2 & -2 \\ -6 & 1 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+(-2){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{3} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 3 & -2 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}5 & 3 & -2 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}5 & 3 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}5 & 3 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-5)\cdot (-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =10(25+9) \\  & =340.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate the value of 
$\,|\begin{aligned}6 & -12 & -2 & -7 \\ 2 & -6 & -2 & -4 \\ -4 & 12 & 7 & 8 \\ -3 & 4 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of ${a}_{21}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*
questions.worked_solution:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the right of ${a}_{21}=2$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}6 & -12 & -2 & -7 \\ 2 & -6 & -2 & -4 \\ -4 & 12 & 7 & 8 \\ -3 & 4 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+3{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+2{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}6 & 6 & 4 & 5 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ -3 & -5 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}6 & 6 & 4 & 5 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ -3 & -5 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}6 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}6 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot (3)\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}6 & 5 \\ -5 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =-6(-24+25) \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$
